title: Storage Rent Rate Card for Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements
content:
Storage rent under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements is quoted on the basis the programme bills on, and the free period, the posted rates, the length of a billing period, the floor under a period's charge and the point at which the rate steps up are all fixed by programme.

## Rates and periods as posted

| Programme | Free days | Daily rate (USD per bushel per day) | Monthly rate (USD per bushel per month) | Basis billed on | Billing period (days) | Period minimum (USD) | Rate steps up after (days) | Step-up (percent) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open Storage Account | 0 | 0.00170 | 0.05100 | per bushel per day | 30 | 10.00 | 180 | 25.0 |
| Grain Bank Deposit Account | 60 | 0.00140 | 0.04200 | per bushel per month | 30 | 12.00 | 240 | 20.0 |
| Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage | 0 | 0.00185 | 0.05550 | per bushel per day | 30 | 25.00 | 270 | 15.0 |
| Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement | 0 | 0.00185 | 0.05550 | flat fee | 30 | 25.00 | 365 | 30.0 |
| Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement | 30 | 0.00210 | 0.06300 | per bushel per month | 30 | 50.00 | 365 | 10.0 |
| Identity Preserved Segregated Storage | 0 | 0.00245 | 0.07350 | per bushel per day | 30 | 75.00 | 365 | 10.0 |

## Reading the card

The free days column is the number of calendar days grain carries free of storage charge from the storage start date; three of the six programmes post no free period at all, one posts 30 days and one posts 60.

The basis column says which of the two posted rates the programme bills on. A programme on the daily basis bills the daily rate; a programme on the monthly basis bills the monthly rate; the one programme on the flat-fee basis bills neither period by period, its storage having been bought up front at the paid-up rate.

The period minimum is the floor under the storage charge for any one billing period on that programme, and ranges from 10.00 on the Open Storage Account to 75.00 on the Identity Preserved Segregated Storage.

The last two columns are the point at which the grain has stood in store long enough for the rate to step up, in calendar days, and the percentage the rate steps up by.

## Matters of judgement

**Does a longer free period always come with a cheaper rate?** No. The Grain Bank Deposit Account carries both the longest free period, at 60 days, and the lowest daily rate, at 0.00170 per bushel per day, while the Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement carries 30 free days at a daily rate of 0.00210. The two columns are set independently, programme by programme.

**Which programme steps up soonest, and by how much?** The Open Storage Account steps up after 180 days and by the largest proportion of the three earliest steppers, 25.0 percent; the Grain Bank Deposit Account steps up after 240 days by 20.0 percent, and the Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage after 270 days by 15.0 percent. The three programmes that step up only after 365 days do so by 30.0 percent, 10.0 percent and 10.0 percent respectively.
